about.title: About HELOC Calculator - Home Equity Line of Credit Tool
about.description: The HELOC Calculator is a home equity financing tool designed to help homeowners estimate credit limits, monthly payments, and costs for Home Equity Lines of Credit. This calculator helps you review available credit, interest-only payments during the draw period, and principal plus interest payments during repayment. Whether you need flexible access to home equity for ongoing expenses or major projects, this tool provides scenario-based HELOC estimates.

howTo.title: How to Use the HELOC Calculator

steps.title: Enter Property Value
steps.description: Input your current home value based on recent appraisal or market analysis.

steps.title: Add Existing Mortgage
steps.description: Enter your current mortgage balance to calculate available equity.

steps.title: Set Credit Limit
steps.description: Determine your desired HELOC credit limit (typically up to 80% LTV).

steps.title: Enter Interest Rate
steps.description: Input the variable interest rate offered by your lender.

steps.title: Set Draw Period
steps.description: Specify the draw period length (typically 10 years) and repayment period.

steps.title: Calculate Payments
steps.description: Review interest-only payments during draw period and full payments during repayment.

tips: HELOCs typically have variable rates that can change over time
During draw period, you may only need to pay interest
Consider rate caps and how payments change during repayment period
Factor in closing costs and annual fees when comparing options

faq.a: A HELOC works like a credit card secured by your home. During the draw period (typically 10 years), you can borrow up to your credit limit and usually pay only interest. During the repayment period (15-20 years), you pay both principal and interest on the outstanding balance.

faq.q: What's the difference between a HELOC and home equity loan?
faq.a: A HELOC provides flexible access to funds with variable rates and interest-only payments during the draw period. A home equity loan provides a lump sum with fixed rates and consistent monthly payments. HELOCs offer flexibility, while home equity loans offer payment predictability.

faq.q: How much can I borrow with a HELOC?
faq.a: Most lenders allow you to borrow up to 80-85% of your home's value minus your existing mortgage balance. For example, if your home is worth $400,000 and you owe $200,000, you might qualify for a HELOC of $120,000-$140,000.

faq.q: Are HELOC interest payments tax deductible?
faq.a: HELOC interest may be tax deductible if you use the funds to buy, build, or substantially improve your home. The deduction is limited to interest on up to $750,000 of qualified residence loans. Review current tax rules for your situation before relying on this treatment.
